newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu ends firmer under low dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu ends firmer under low dollar demand.

text.p: Romania's leu currency closed firmer at 6,700/7,000 to the dollar on Thursday against some 6,800/7,000 at opening with dollar demand easing and leu shortages still affecting some banks, traders said.
Quotes on banks' screens continued to show wide ranges with leu-dollar prices between 6,200/100 to 7,200/8,400.
On Thursday quotes of state-run Bancorex showed large shifts, edging up and down at close, with leu-dollar rates between 6,900/7,000 to 8,400/500.
Dealers were puzzled by the shifting quotes of Bancorex, which takes an estimated 30 percent of market turnover, and said Bancorex did not seem to have had any interbank deals on Thursday.
"I don't know what their game is because when we ask for a quote they usually fail to answer," said one trader with a private bank.
Most operators said declining energy imports and purchasing power and attractive deposit rates gave the leu enough strength to resist attempts to push the greenback higher.
"The leu is so well backed that any steps to push it below 7,000 have failed," said one trader.

Tougher monetary policies sent bank deposit rates to up to 150 percent annually, while inflation running at 18.8 percent in February has halved purchasing power of most Romanians who earn about $80 per month.
Short-term prices lingered near 230 percent with the money market awaiting the results of the central bank (BNR) auction for one-week refinancing funds due later on Thursday.
The BNR cut its offer to 600 billion lei from a previous 660 billion, while keeping the minimum permitted rate unchanged at 226 percent.
Leu-dollar retail prices weakened slightly to 7,450/800 against 7,300/800 in early trading.
